correlates.name: Diabetic Vascular Disease
correlates.presentation: In this model the ROS stain is the readout; clinically the same process is the endothelial dysfunction of diabetes.
correlates.pathophysiology: Slide 6 shows arteries from pre-diabetic and diabetic rats stained red for reactive oxygen species (ROS). A healthy VSMC does not generate ROS — it only contracts and relaxes — so the stain itself marks a switched, unhealthy phenotype.

correlates.name: Atherosclerosis: VSMC, the Fibrous Cap, and Plaque Rupture
correlates.presentation: A ruptured fibrous cap with an overlying occluding thrombus — the acute coronary event.
correlates.pathophysiology: As plaque progresses, medial VSMCs lose the contractile phenotype and become synthetic.

correlates.name: In-Stent Restenosis
correlates.presentation: Recurrent ischemic symptoms weeks to months after stenting, with a re-occluded lumen.
correlates.pathophysiology: A stent holds the lumen open but the metal damages the endothelium. Less endothelium means less nitric oxide, and NO is both a vasodilator and an anti-proliferative brake on the underlying VSMC.

correlates.name: Hypertension and L-Type Calcium Channel Blockers
correlates.pathophysiology: Excess vasoconstriction raises peripheral resistance and blood pressure. VSMC contraction depends on extracellular Ca²⁺ entering through voltage-gated L-type channels.
correlates.treatment: Nifedipine, amlodipine, verapamil — all L-type calcium channel blockers. Blocking the channel means the calcium never arrives, so there is no Ca²⁺-calmodulin complex and no contraction.

correlates.name: Hypertensive Crisis in a Patient with Endothelial Dysfunction
correlates.pathophysiology: In diabetes the endothelium is dysfunctional and produces less nitric oxide, so endothelium-dependent vasodilators lose potency. Sodium nitroprusside bypasses the endothelium entirely by donating NO straight to the VSMC.
correlates.treatment: Sodium nitroprusside, a very potent vasodilator used in the emergency department for hypertensive crisis.
